kurz: Which risks justify insurance, which four policies cover the risks that threaten your livelihood, and which policies you can do without.

bloecke.md:
Insurance is an exchange, not a savings contract. The insured person pays a small, certain amount and in return receives the promise that a large, uncertain amount will not hit their household. The price of this promise is made up of the expected loss plus loadings for administration, distribution and profit margin. Across the insured pool as a whole, policyholders therefore inevitably pay in more than they get out, because otherwise no insurer could survive.

This gives rise to the most important rule when choosing insurance. Losses that can be paid from the emergency fund or from two months' salary are ones you bear yourself. The reason is that the loading for administration and distribution is highest in percentage terms for small losses. A policy for a device worth €800 therefore mainly offers convenience and hardly any additional security.

The question is what happens to your household if a loss occurs. The probability of the loss is not decisive for this. You do not insure a risk you can bear yourself. You insure a risk you cannot bear even if it is very unlikely.

bloecke.titel: Risks by size of loss and probability
bloecke.unter: Only the bottom-right quadrant justifies a policy. Most of the policies sold cover risks from the top-left quadrant.

felder.text: Cracked screen, glasses, bicycle, pane of glass. Happens often, costs little. In the end the premium is higher than the sum of the losses.
Need for long-term care in old age. When the loss is almost certain to occur, the premium approaches the loss. Saving up helps more than insuring here.
Travel luggage, lost keys, mobile phone theft on holiday. Rare and small. Any policy for these is pure cost.
Bodily injury, occupational disability, death of the main earner, serious illness, house fire. Rare, but they destroy livelihoods.

bloecke.md:
## Compulsory insurance and voluntary policies

In Germany, the law requires health and long-term care insurance (statutory or private), motor third-party liability insurance for motor vehicles designed to travel faster than 6 km/h and, for most employees, statutory pension, unemployment and accident insurance. On top of this, there is compulsory insurance for certain groups, such as dog owners' liability insurance in several federal states. All other insurance is voluntary and is therefore sold particularly hard.

Four policies cover the risks that can ruin a household financially: [[personal liability insurance (Privathaftpflicht)]], [[occupational disability insurance (Berufsunfähigkeitsversicherung)]], term life insurance if someone depends on your income, and health insurance, which is compulsory anyway but may have been chosen badly. A household that has these four policies and no others is better protected than the average.

## Personal liability insurance

Statutory liability under Section 823 BGB (Civil Code) is unlimited in amount. If someone knocks a cyclist over and causes permanent paraplegia, they owe medical treatment, lifelong care, lost lifetime earnings and compensation for pain and suffering. For a young victim, this adds up to millions over the decades. Without insurance, the person responsible is liable with their present and future assets, and the seizable part of their income is then tied up for decades.

A blanket cover of €50 million is recommended, plus at least 10 million per injured person and one million for pure financial losses. Good policies cost single people about €30 to €39 a year, families around €46 to €103 depending on the scope, and couples over 60 sometimes as little as €27. A family policy also covers partners and children until the end of their first vocational training or degree. Dogs and horses are not covered. They need their own animal owner's liability insurance, which is compulsory for dogs in several federal states anyway. Cats and small pets, on the other hand, are covered.

With an annual premium of €35 and cover of €50 million, around €1.4 million of cover is available for every euro paid in. This ratio is possible because losses running into millions are rare, and for the same reason the policy is so cheap. A lower sum insured typically saves only a few euros a year and in return limits protection for the very large losses the policy is meant for.

## Occupational disability

For anyone in work, their future earning capacity is by far their largest asset. A 30-year-old employee with €3,000 net will earn around €1.33 million in purely nominal terms by the age of 67 (37 years times twelve months times €3,000), without counting any pay rises. Nobody would leave a portfolio of this size uninsured, yet their own earning capacity often remains unprotected.

About one in four people in work becomes occupationally disabled at least once during their working life. This order of magnitude is often quoted, but the basis of calculation varies depending on the source. The distribution of causes is more revealing than the exact rate.

bloecke.titel: Causes of occupational disability (shares of existing claims, 2026)
bloecke.unter: Around 93% of cases are due to illness. Other analyses put accidents at just over 7%, which does not change this conclusion.

bloecke.md:
State protection for this case is limited. After six weeks of continued pay from the employer, the health insurance fund pays sickness benefit (Krankengeld). It amounts to around 70% of gross pay, at most 90% of net pay, and is paid for a maximum of 72 further weeks (78 weeks within three years minus the six weeks, Section 48 SGB V, Social Code Book V). After that, this protection ends.

Then only the statutory reduced earning capacity pension (Erwerbsminderungsrente) remains. It requires that your capacity to work is below six hours a day in any occupation at all, not just in the one you trained for. The full pension is only paid if this capacity is below three hours; between three and six hours, only the partial reduced earning capacity pension is paid (Section 43 SGB VI, Social Code Book VI). In 2023, the full reduced earning capacity pension averaged €1,059 a month, the partial one €593. More than 40% of applications are rejected.

The statutory reduced earning capacity pension is no substitute for occupational disability insurance, because it does not take into account the occupation you trained for. A roofer who could still sit at a reception desk for six hours a day therefore receives nothing.

Private accident insurance is no substitute for disability insurance either. Accidents cause only about 6% to 7% of occupational disability cases, and only just over 1% of all severe disabilities are due to an accident or an occupational disease. Basic abilities (Grundfähigkeit), dread disease and multi-risk policies usually do not cover the most common trigger, mental illness, either. They are a second choice for people who cannot get disability insurance. For everyone else, disability insurance is the first choice.

bloecke.titel: Premiums for disability insurance (range depends mainly on occupation)
zeilen: Range across all occupations, ages and end ages

bloecke.md:
The usual target for the disability benefit is around 80% of your last net salary. The lower limit is a monthly benefit of about €1,000. In an emergency, a lower benefit is largely offset against basic income support (Grundsicherung) and then brings hardly any extra money. At the upper end, insurers usually require a medical examination from a monthly benefit of about €2,500.

When choosing a policy, the terms and conditions matter more than the premium. Indispensable features are a waiver of the [[abstract referral clause (abstrakte Verweisung)]] (otherwise the insurer can refer you to another occupation that you could theoretically be expected to do), a [[guaranteed insurability option]] without a new health assessment for marriage, the birth of a child or a property purchase, retrospective benefits for at least three years, a forecast period of six months instead of the statutory definition “likely to be permanent” (Section 172 VVG, Insurance Contract Act), no deferred period, deferral of premiums in case of payment difficulties and no obligation to report a change of occupation. The range on offer is wide. For 2026, 636 policies and policy combinations from 59 companies were rated, 537 of them with the top grade.

Health questions must be answered completely and truthfully. If the pre-contractual duty of disclosure is breached, the insurer can refuse to pay or withdraw from the contract. This happens when a claim is made, that is, when the money is needed. The patient receipt (Patientenquittung) from the health insurance fund and copies of your medical records from recent years are helpful.

Instead of applying directly to the insurer, it is advisable to start with an **anonymous risk pre-enquiry** through a broker. A rejected enquiry made under your name can be stored in the insurers' warning and information system (Hinweis- und Informationssystem) and make every further application more difficult. Just under 80% of applications are accepted without restrictions, around 10.5% with benefit exclusions and 2.8% with a risk surcharge, and 2.75% are rejected. According to a 2025 study, just under 80% of claims were likewise approved. About 39% of the rejections occurred because policyholders stopped responding after submitting their claim.

## Term life insurance

Term life insurance pays a fixed sum to surviving dependants and does not build up any capital. It is necessary for main or sole earners with a family and for couples with an outstanding mortgage loan. For single people without maintenance obligations it is superfluous, because there is then nobody whose standard of living depends on the insured person's income.

The rule of thumb for the sum insured is three to five times gross annual salary, plus the outstanding balance of any mortgage loan. For the same profile, providers' prices differ considerably, by up to a factor of three in comparisons. Because the benefit is standardised, comparing is more worthwhile here than for almost any other policy. Suicide is usually covered once the policy has been in force for three years.

bloecke.titel: Sum insured by rule of thumb (plus the outstanding balance of a loan)

bloecke.md:
## Health insurance

In statutory health insurance (GKV), the general contribution rate under Section 241 SGB V is 14.6%. On top of this comes an additional contribution (Zusatzbeitrag), which each fund sets itself. For 2026, an average additional contribution of 2.9% was set (in 2025 it was 2.5%). At the start of 2026, the funds open nationwide charged between 2.18% and 4.39%. The total contribution rate therefore ranges from 16.78% to 18.99%. Income is subject to contributions up to the contribution assessment ceiling (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze) of €5,812.50 a month.

The range of around 2.2 contribution rate points is probably the easiest saving in the entire field of insurance. At the contribution assessment ceiling it corresponds to around €128 in total contributions a month. For employees, who pay half the contribution, that is just over €64 a month or about €770 a year. The catalogue of benefits is largely identical. The funds differ in the extra benefits set out in their statutes (Satzungsleistungen) and in service, not in the compulsory statutory benefits.

Switching to private health insurance (PKV) is possible if gross pay is above the compulsory insurance threshold (Versicherungspflichtgrenze). In 2026 this threshold is €6,450 a month or €77,400 a year. The most important difference concerns the premium. The GKV contribution depends on income and is capped by the contribution assessment ceiling. The PKV premium depends on your state of health when you join and on your age, and it must still be paid in retirement, when income falls.

The Association of Private Health Insurers (Verband der privaten Krankenversicherung) reported an average premium for 2025 of €536 a month for adults without an entitlement to state healthcare allowance (Beihilfe). In the Beihilfe tariffs for civil servants, it was well below €350 in all age groups. Individual premiums are often higher. For civil servants entitled to state healthcare allowance (Beihilfe), PKV is usually the right choice. Employees should bear in mind that returning to GKV from the age of 55 is practically impossible. In addition, family members without their own income each cost a separate premium in PKV, whereas in GKV they are covered free of charge. Commission-free fee-based advice costs €150 to €200 per hour, for a total of at least six hours. For a decision that is binding for decades, that is a small amount.

## Dispensable and supplementary insurance

Mobile phone, glasses, travel luggage, glass and funeral expenses insurance as well as education insurance policies are of low priority or superfluous. Legal expenses insurance is a borderline case. In a survey from the end of 2023, only 23% of respondents had been involved in court proceedings within ten years, whether as claimant, defendant or witness. Against this, a single person pays an annual premium of €240 to €680, plus waiting periods of usually three months and exclusions for, among other things, family and inheritance law cases and investments.

Two policies, on the other hand, are worth considering even though they are not among the four existential policies. For property owners, this is buildings insurance with natural hazards cover, because without this add-on, flooding, heavy rain and landslides are not covered. The second policy is travel health insurance. It costs from about €10 a year and covers treatment and medically necessary repatriation, which statutory health insurance does not pay for abroad or pays for only in part.

bloecke.titel: Annual premiums compared (lower end of each surveyed range)
bloecke.unter: The size of the premium says nothing about importance. The cheapest and the most expensive item both belong to the recommended cover, while the legal expenses insurance in between is dispensable for most people.

bloecke.md:
With an [[Excess (insurance)|excess]], the policyholder bears small losses themselves. This makes sense because handling a €200 claim costs the insurer almost as much as the loss itself. The premium falls accordingly.

Suppose a policy costs €400 a year, and an excess of €250 lowers the premium by 15%, that is, by €60 a year. After just over four claim-free years, a single excess is offset by the savings, and from the fifth year onwards the saving stays with the policyholder. The calculation only becomes unfavourable with more than one claim every four years, and with claims that frequent the policyholder loses the contract anyway. In practice, almost all recommended liability and legal expenses policies provide for an excess of €150 to €250.

## Endowment policies

Endowment policies and conventional private pension insurance combine risk cover with building up capital. They are hardly suitable as an investment. The maximum technical interest rate (Höchstrechnungszins), usually called the guaranteed interest rate in sales, has been 1.0% since 1 January 2025 (Section 2 DeckRV, Actuarial Reserves Ordinance). It applies only to the savings portion that remains after deducting acquisition, administration and risk costs, not to the entire premium. According to Assekurata, the current rate of interest credited on new endowment policies averaged 2.54% across the market in 2026. In a study of 30 life insurers, however, the effective return on premiums of conventional pension insurance averaged 0.14% and was negative for some providers. That is the most recent documented comparison figure. The order of magnitude has not shifted in the products' favour since then.

Taxation comes on top. The payout is completely tax-free only for policies taken out by 31 December 2004. For policies taken out from 2005 onwards, the investment gain is taxable, but only half of it if paid out after the age of 62 and after a term of at least twelve years. For policies from 2005 to 2011, reaching the age of 60 is sufficient for this.

A monthly premium of €200 over 30 years adds up to total premiums of €72,000. For policies from 2015 onwards, at most 2.5% of this may be charged through the Zillmer adjustment (Zillmerung), that is, offset against the first premiums straight away, which here means €1,800 (maximum Zillmer rate under Section 4 DeckRV; before 2015 it was 4%). This limit only applies to the Zillmer adjustment; the agreed acquisition costs can be higher. For the surrender value, the acquisition costs of policies from 2008 onwards must be spread over the first five years (Section 169 VVG). The €1,800 alone amounts to €30 a month over 60 months, that is, 15% of every premium in the first five years, before anything earns interest. This is why the surrender value is well below the amounts paid in during the first years.

links.titel: Risk cover and investment kept separate
punkte: The premium for term life and disability insurance is a pure price for risk
The investment can be terminated and transferred at any time
Costs are visible and can be compared individually
When your life situation changes, only the component affected is adjusted

rechts.titel: Cover and investment in one policy
punkte: Risk, administration and distribution costs cannot be separated within the premium
Cancelling ends cover and investment at the same time
Surrender value well below the amounts paid in during the first years
If one part no longer fits, the other is affected too

bloecke.md: The criticism of new policies does not apply to old ones. Policies taken out between the mid-1980s and June 2000 usually have a guaranteed interest rate of 3.5% or 4.0% on the savings portion, which from today's perspective is a good investment. For policies taken out from July 2000 to the end of 2003, it is 3.25%. In addition, on early surrender the non-guaranteed terminal bonus is lost entirely, and it can account for about a fifth of the total return. If you need money, a premium reduction or making the policy paid-up should therefore be considered first. An existing disability or term life policy should never be cancelled before the replacement policy has been issued. Between application and acceptance there is a new health assessment, and its result gets worse with every year of age.

schritte.titel: List existing policies and sort them by maximum loss
schritte.text: Write down all policies one below the other with annual premium, sum insured and notice period. Then check for each policy whether the loss could be covered from savings. Every policy for which this is true goes on the list for cancellation.

schritte.titel: Check or take out personal liability insurance
schritte.text: Blanket cover of €50 million if possible, family members included, damage caused while doing someone a favour and bad debt cover (Forderungsausfall) included. A dog or horse needs a separate policy.

schritte.titel: Prepare disability insurance with an anonymous risk pre-enquiry
schritte.text: Gather your patient receipt and medical records beforehand. Assess the terms and conditions before the premium. Target level around 80% of net pay, not below about €1,000.

schritte.titel: Term life insurance only if others depend on you financially
schritte.text: With a partner, children or an outstanding mortgage loan, insure three to five times gross annual salary plus the outstanding debt and compare providers. Otherwise, no policy is needed.

schritte.titel: Compare health insurance funds, add travel health cover
schritte.text: Switching funds can save around €770 a year at the contribution assessment ceiling, with the same catalogue of compulsory benefits.

schritte.titel: Only cancel once the replacement is in place
schritte.text: Minor insurance policies can be cancelled immediately, existential policies only once the new contract has been accepted in writing.

mitnehmen: Only losses that would ruin the household are insured. Anything that can be paid from the emergency fund stays uninsured, because the cost loading is highest for small losses.
For about €30 to €40 a year, personal liability insurance covers a statutory liability that is unlimited in amount. No other policy offers a comparable ratio of premium to cover.

Around 93% of occupational disability is caused by illness, most often mental illness. Accident insurance and the statutory reduced earning capacity pension are therefore no substitute for disability insurance.

With disability insurance, the terms matter more than the premium, above all the waiver of the abstract referral clause, a guaranteed insurability option, a six-month forecast period and retrospective benefits.
Risk cover and investment belong in separate contracts. The exception is old policies with a guaranteed interest rate of 3.5% or 4.0%, which should at most be made paid-up and not cancelled.

begriffe.text: Voluntary insurance against the statutory liability under Section 823 BGB, which is unlimited in amount. It covers bodily injury, property damage and pure financial losses caused to third parties. A blanket cover of €50 million is recommended.

Insurance that pays an agreed monthly benefit if you are expected to be able to pursue your most recent occupation only to an extent of less than 50% for at least six months. It protects lifetime income, not health.

A clause that allows the insurer to refer the insured person to another occupation they could theoretically be expected to do and to refuse benefits, even if they do not work in that occupation. Good policies waive it.
The right to increase the insured benefit on certain occasions, such as marriage, the birth of a child, a big pay rise or buying property, without a new health assessment.

The maximum interest rate permitted under supervisory law that life insurers may use to calculate guaranteed benefits (Section 2 DeckRV). Since 2025 it has been 1.0%, and it applies only to the savings portion after costs, not to the entire premium.
An agreed amount the policyholder pays per claim. It lowers the premium, because small claims, which are expensive to process, are no longer settled through the policy.
